newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee firms on lack of import covering.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee firms on lack of import covering.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee opened stronger against the dollar on Tuesday and was expected to remain firm on a lack of commercial demand for the greenback, dealers said.
At 0445 GMT the rupee was at 58.42 to the dollar after opening at the 58.40. On Monday, it closed at 58.45.
The Central Bank, going by the international weakening of the dollar, pushed the greenback down by 1.5 local cents and fixed buying and selling at 58.3976 and 59.5774.
"Overseas the dollar is down and the forecast seems to be that it will be under considerable pressure during the next few days," said an American Express Bank dealer.
Dealers said the market has been at the bottom for the past three weeks primarily due to the lack of import covering.
"People's consumption patterns have changed due to money being tight. A slowing down in consumption has cut down imports," said a foreign bank dealer.
But other dealers said all that could change instantly.
"Imports are very limited these days. So the dollar is at the bottom," a Standard Chartered Bank dealer said.
"But (the dollar) could pick up instantly. All it takes is one big (import) bill to push it up," he said.
Overnight call money rate was at its opening level of 12 percent, dealers said. -- Colombo newsroom (941) 434319
